advances: Principal-pivot covers exist for every finite nonempty lattice, but even the smallest weighted profile among all principal-pivot subcovers need not be bounded independently of dimension. The family below has minimum profile exactly \(2+\lfloor m/2\rfloor4^{-1/3}\), while every original affine law on its entire convex lattice census has positive dimension-independent normalized second and third depth moments. Thus the obstruction concerns this cover interface, and does not disprove the locked conjecture or an actual moment inequality.

proof:
First verify the complete census, for any finite nonempty lattice \(P\). In fact this step works for any finite poset. Put
$$
K_P=\lbrace x\in[0,2]^P:
 x_u-x_v\le1\text{ for all distinct }u,v\in P
                        \text{ with }u\not<_P v\rbrace.
\tag{3}
$$
This is compact and convex. The all-one point satisfies every box and difference inequality strictly, so \(K_P\) has nonempty interior in \(\mathbb R^P\). An integral point of the box has ternary coordinates, and within those coordinates \(x_u-x_v>1\) is equivalent to \(x_u=2,x_v=0\). Thus \(K_P\cap\mathbb Z^P=D_P\), including all boundary points. Also \(D_P\subset\operatorname{conv}(D_P)\subset K_P\), so \(\operatorname{conv}(D_P)\cap\mathbb Z^P=D_P\). This proves completeness without deleting any lattice point.

For any ternary assignment \(x\), write \(A_2(x)=\lbrace u:x_u=2\rbrace\) and \(A_0(x)=\lbrace u:x_u=0\rbrace\). Directly from the coordinate definition,
$$
x\in E_v
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
u\le_P v\text{ for every }u\in A_2(x)
\ \text{ and }\
v\le_P w\text{ for every }w\in A_0(x).
\tag{4}
$$
Indeed, the value 1 is allowed at every coordinate, the value 2 is allowed precisely on the nonstrict downset of \(v\), and the value 0 precisely on its nonstrict upset. If \(x\in E_v\), any coordinate \(u\) carrying 2 and any coordinate \(w\) carrying 0 satisfy \(u\le_P v\le_P w\). They are distinct because they carry different values, hence \(u<_P w\). Therefore \(E_v\subset D_P\).

Conversely, take \(x\in D_P\). Finite nonempty lattices have a bottom and a top. With the conventions that the join of an empty set is the bottom and the meet of an empty set is the top, put
\(r=\bigvee A_2(x)\) and \(s=\bigwedge A_0(x)\). If both sets are nonempty, every member of \(A_0(x)\) is an upper bound for every member of \(A_2(x)\), so \(r\le_P s\). If either set is empty, the same inequality follows from the stated bottom or top convention. Choose \(v=r\), which lies in the interval \([r,s]\). Every 2-coordinate is at most \(v\), and every 0-coordinate is at least \(v\). Equation (4) gives \(x\in E_v\). This includes no 2s, no 0s, and the all-one assignment, proving the full pivot cover.

The factors at the incomparable coordinates are singletons. Every other nonpivot factor is binary, and the pivot factor is ternary. There are \(N-\operatorname{inc}_P(v)-1\) such binary factors. This proves both the fixed-coordinate count and the stated cardinality of each \(E_v\). Each component is itself exactly the integer census of the product of its coordinate intervals.

Now consider \(P_m\). The specified relations give a partial order: the chain relations are transitive, and the only strict relations involving \(b\) are \(o<b<t\). Two comparable elements have their smaller and larger elements as meet and join. The only incomparable pairs are \(a_i,b\); their sole common lower bound is \(o\) and their sole common upper bound is \(t\). Their meet and join are therefore \(o,t\). This proves that \(P_m\) is a lattice for every \(m\ge2\).

Its incomparable counts and pivot sizes are exactly
$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{inc}(o)=\operatorname{inc}(t)&=0,
&|E_o|=|E_t|&=3\cdot2^{m+2},\\
\operatorname{inc}(a_i)&=1\quad(1\le i\le m),
&|E_{a_i}|&=3\cdot2^{m+1},\\
\operatorname{inc}(b)&=m,
&|E_b|&=12.
\end{aligned}
\tag{5}
$$
In particular each chain pivot has exactly one fixed coordinate, namely \(b\); the pivot \(b\) has exactly the \(m\) chain coordinates fixed. Formula (5) gives the full profile in the statement.

We prove the characterization of all subcovers. The all-zero assignment belongs to \(D_{P_m}\) and only to \(E_o\): for any other pivot \(v\), the coordinate \(o<v\) is in its strict downset and cannot be 0. Similarly the all-two assignment belongs only to \(E_t\), since for any other pivot \(v\), its strict upset contains \(t\), where 2 is forbidden. Every subcover must therefore include \(o,t\).

For each \(1\le i<m\), define \(w^{(i)}\) to have value 2 at \(a_i\), value 0 at \(a_{i+1}\), and value 1 everywhere else. It belongs to \(D_{P_m}\), since its sole 2-label is strictly below its sole 0-label. By (4),
\(w^{(i)}\in E_v\) if and only if \(a_i\le v\le a_{i+1}\). This interval consists exactly of \(a_i,a_{i+1}\). Thus every subcover must select at least one endpoint of each displayed path edge. Neither \(b\), \(o\), nor \(t\) can cover these witnesses.

For sufficiency, suppose \(\mathcal J\) contains \(o,t\) and meets every path edge. Take \(x\in D_{P_m}\). If \(x\in E_o\cup E_t\), it is already covered. Otherwise there is a 2-coordinate other than \(o\) and a 0-coordinate other than \(t\). Every such 2-label must be strictly below every such 0-label. The only strict relations with lower endpoint different from \(o\) and upper endpoint different from \(t\) are \(a_i<a_j\) with \(i<j\). Hence all these labels are chain labels; in particular \(x_b=1\). Let \(i\) be the largest index of a chain coordinate carrying 2, and let \(j\) be the smallest index of a chain coordinate carrying 0. Both exist and \(i<j\). Since \(\mathcal J\) meets \(\lbrace a_i,a_{i+1}\rbrace\), it contains some \(a_k\) with \(i\le k\le j\). Every 2-label of \(x\) is then at most \(a_k\), and every 0-label at least \(a_k\). Equation (4) yields \(x\in E_{a_k}\). This proves sufficiency, with no condition on selecting \(b\).

The disjoint edges \(\lbrace a_1,a_2\rbrace,\lbrace a_3,a_4\rbrace,\ldots\) force at least \(\lfloor m/2\rfloor\) chain pivots. The even-indexed set
\(\lbrace a_2,a_4,\ldots,a_{2\lfloor m/2\rfloor}\rbrace\) meets every path edge and attains this number. Each chain pivot has weight \(4^{-1/3}\), the forced pivots \(o,t\) each have weight 1, and the optional pivot \(b\) has strictly positive weight. These facts prove the exact minimum (1), including \(m=2\).

It remains to establish the actual moment calibration. Partition the entire census by the three coordinates \(o,b,t\). Let \(\mathcal B\subset\lbrace0,1,2\rbrace^3\) be the set of supported triples \(\beta=(\beta_o,\beta_b,\beta_t)\); it is nonempty and has at most 27 members. For each such triple, the inequalities involving only these fixed coordinates already hold. Their order is \(o<b<t\), so a triple is supported exactly when its own 2-labels lie strictly below its own 0-labels: the all-one assignment on the chain coordinates extends every such triple.

For a supported \(\beta\), define its common coordinate mask \(I_\beta\) on all \(a_i\) as follows. Forbid the value 2 if \(\beta_o=0\) or \(\beta_b=0\). Forbid the value 0 if \(\beta_t=2\) or \(\beta_b=2\). Allow 1 in every case. Thus \(I_\beta\) is respectively
\(\lbrace0,1,2\rbrace\), \(\lbrace0,1\rbrace\), \(\lbrace1,2\rbrace\), or \(\lbrace1\rbrace\), according to whether neither, only 2, only 0, or both extremes are forbidden.

The residual support is exactly \(D_m\cap I_\beta^m\), where \(D_m\) is the ordered-chain support of accepted fact 3db95e3d61a4eedf, indexed here by \(a_1,\ldots,a_m\). To verify this without omitting cross constraints, a chain 2 is incompatible with a fixed 0 at \(o\) or \(b\), and is compatible with a fixed 0 at \(t\). A chain 0 is incompatible with a fixed 2 at \(t\) or \(b\), and is compatible with a fixed 2 at \(o\). Fixed coordinates equal to 1 impose no condition, and a chain coordinate equal to 1 imposes no condition. These are all pairs involving a fixed and a free coordinate. The remaining free-coordinate condition is precisely that every chain 2 precedes every chain 0. This proves necessity and sufficiency of the residual support description. In particular it is the full \(D_m\), a full binary cube \(\lbrace0,1\rbrace^m\), a full binary cube \(\lbrace1,2\rbrace^m\), or the singleton \(\lbrace\mathbf1\rbrace\); the chain condition is vacuous in the last three cases.

Write \(\iota_\beta(z)\in\mathbb R^{P_m}\) for insertion of \(\beta\) at \(o,b,t\) and \(z_i\) at \(a_i\). Put
$$
\begin{aligned}
Z_\beta&=\sum_{z\in D_m\cap I_\beta^m}
                 e^{\sum_{i=1}^m\ell_{a_i}z_i},
&
q_\beta(z)&=\frac{e^{\sum_{i=1}^m\ell_{a_i}z_i}}{Z_\beta},\\
\alpha_\beta
 &=\frac{e^{\ell_o\beta_o+\ell_b\beta_b+\ell_t\beta_t}Z_\beta}{Z},
&
p_{\iota_\beta(z)}&=\alpha_\beta q_\beta(z).
\end{aligned}
\tag{6}
$$
These \(\alpha_\beta\) are the original marginal masses, are positive, and sum to one. In particular (6) retains the original global \(Z\), and the conditional fields are exactly the original fields restricted to the chain.

Use \(\tau_{q_\beta}\) for the depth of the conditional law with respect to all containing closed halfspaces in \(\mathbb R^m\). If the support is \(D_m\), accepted fact 3db95e3d61a4eedf, with its dimension \(n=m\), field \((\ell_{a_i})_{i=1}^m\), and its original-field normalization now \(Z_\beta\), gives \(M_2(q_\beta)\ge c_2 4^{-m}\). If the support is one of the binary cubes, \(q_\beta\) is a product of binary affine laws. Every containing halfspace contains the target atom, so \(\tau_{q_\beta}(z)\ge q_\beta(z)\). Consequently
$$
M_2(q_\beta)\ge\sum_zq_\beta(z)^3
 =\prod_{i=1}^m\bigl[s_i^3+(1-s_i)^3\bigr]
 \ge4^{-m},
\tag{7}
$$
where \(s_i,1-s_i\) are the two probabilities at coordinate \(i\), and
\(s_i^3+(1-s_i)^3=1/4+3(s_i-1/2)^2\). For the singleton support, the depth and the moment are 1. Finally \(0<c_2<1\), since \(0<\log(1+3\tanh^2(1/32))<\log4<2\). Thus in every case \(M_2(q_\beta)\ge c_2 4^{-m}\).

For the ambient transfer, fix any target \(x=\iota_\beta(z)\) and any original ambient closed halfspace \(H\subset\mathbb R^{P_m}\) containing it. The inverse image \(\iota_\beta^{-1}(H)\) is either a closed halfspace in \(\mathbb R^m\) containing \(z\), or all of \(\mathbb R^m\) if its restricted normal vanishes. It cannot be empty because \(x\in H\). Its \(q_\beta\)-mass is therefore at least \(\tau_{q_\beta}(z)\). Retaining only the mass in this stratum gives
\(p(H)\ge\alpha_\beta q_\beta(\iota_\beta^{-1}(H))
\ge\alpha_\beta\tau_{q_\beta}(z)\).
Taking the infimum over all the original ambient containing halfspaces yields
\(\tau_p(\iota_\beta(z))\ge\alpha_\beta\tau_{q_\beta}(z)\).

The strata are disjoint and exhaust the entire census. Therefore their target contributions can be summed without duplication, giving
$$
\begin{aligned}
M_2(p)
&\ge\sum_{\beta\in\mathcal B}\alpha_\beta^3 M_2(q_\beta)\\
&\ge c_2 4^{-m}\sum_{\beta\in\mathcal B}\alpha_\beta^3\\
&\ge \frac{c_2}{729}4^{-m}
 =\frac{64c_2}{729}4^{-N}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{8}
$$
For the third line, if \(k=|\mathcal B|\le27\), Jensen's inequality and \(\sum_\beta\alpha_\beta=1\) give \(\sum_\beta\alpha_\beta^3\ge k^{-2}\ge27^{-2}\). The last equality uses the exact ambient dimension \(N=m+3\). This includes all supported triples, all binary masks, and the singleton residual support.

Finally Jensen's inequality under the entire original law gives
\(M_3(p)=\mathbb E_p[(\tau_p^2)^{3/2}]\ge M_2(p)^{3/2}\).
Combining this with (8) proves (2) with the stated normalization and all original ambient containing halfspaces.
statement:
For a finite nonempty lattice \(P\), write \(N=|P|\), and use the elements of \(P\) as coordinate labels in \(\mathbb R^P\). Define
$$
D_P=\lbrace x\in\lbrace0,1,2\rbrace^P:
       x_u=2,\ x_v=0\Longrightarrow u<_P v\rbrace,
\qquad
\operatorname{inc}_P(v)=
 \bigl|\lbrace u\in P:u\text{ is incomparable with }v\rbrace\bigr|.
$$
For each pivot \(v\in P\), define the Cartesian product \(E_v\) by allowing \(\lbrace1,2\rbrace\) on its strict downset, \(\lbrace0,1\rbrace\) on its strict upset, \(\lbrace0,1,2\rbrace\) at \(v\), and \(\lbrace1\rbrace\) on every incomparable coordinate.

Then \(D_P\) is the complete lattice census of a full-dimensional compact convex polytope in \(\mathbb R^P\), and \(D_P=\bigcup_{v\in P}E_v\). Every \(E_v\) has exactly \(\operatorname{inc}_P(v)\) fixed coordinates and cardinality \(3\cdot2^{N-\operatorname{inc}_P(v)-1}\).

For each integer \(m\ge2\), take the particular order \(P_m\) with bottom \(o\), top \(t\), and remaining elements \(a_1,\ldots,a_m,b\), where
\(o<a_1<\cdots<a_m<t\), \(o<b<t\), and \(b\) is incomparable with every \(a_i\). It is a lattice and has \(N=m+3\) elements. Its full pivot profile is
\(2+m4^{-1/3}+4^{-m/3}\).

More precisely, a set \(\mathcal J\subset P_m\) satisfies
\(D_{P_m}=\bigcup_{v\in\mathcal J}E_v\) if and only if \(o,t\in\mathcal J\) and \(\mathcal J\cap\lbrace a_1,\ldots,a_m\rbrace\) meets every pair \(\lbrace a_i,a_{i+1}\rbrace\), \(1\le i<m\). Membership of \(b\) in \(\mathcal J\) is optional. Consequently
$$
\min_{\substack{\mathcal J\subset P_m\\
                 D_{P_m}=\bigcup_{v\in\mathcal J}E_v}}
       \ \sum_{v\in\mathcal J}4^{-\operatorname{inc}_{P_m}(v)/3}
 =2+\lfloor m/2\rfloor4^{-1/3}\longrightarrow\infty.
\tag{1}
$$
In particular, no absolute upper bound for this profile can hold for some choice of principal-pivot subcover of every finite lattice census.

For the actual moment calibration, let
$$
c_2=\frac{\bigl[\log(1+3\tanh^2(1/32))\bigr]^3}{3456},
\qquad
c_{\mathrm{lat}}=\frac{64c_2}{729}>0.
$$
The constant \(c_2\) is exactly that of accepted fact 3db95e3d61a4eedf. For any \(m\ge2\) and any \(\ell\in\mathbb R^{P_m}\), retain the entire census and its original normalization:
$$
Z=\sum_{x\in D_{P_m}}e^{\ell\cdot x},\qquad
p_x=\frac{e^{\ell\cdot x}}{Z},\qquad
\tau_p(x)=
 \inf_{\substack{H\subset\mathbb R^{P_m}\text{ closed halfspace}\\x\in H}}
       \ \sum_{y\in D_{P_m}\cap H}p_y,
\qquad
M_q(p)=\sum_{x\in D_{P_m}}p_x\tau_p(x)^q.
$$
All containing halfspaces with arbitrary nonzero normal are allowed, including boundary targets. Then
$$
M_2(p)\ge c_{\mathrm{lat}}4^{-N},
\qquad
M_3(p)\ge c_{\mathrm{lat}}^{3/2}8^{-N}.
\tag{2}
$$
There is no restriction on the signs, magnitudes, or order of the fields.
